ST-178 and SUG-178: one AI label component

The on-site badge (SUG-178, #57) and the baked mark (ST-178, #178) are one component, .aiLabel: same anchor, type, padding, border and fill. Rules below decide what it says and how it behaves. Images are stand-ins. The mark is shown as the same label rasterised into the file.

1. Can both show at once?

No. Never two visible labels. The HTML label always sits on the exact spot the baked mark occupies and is never smaller than it, so it covers the baked one. A reader sees one label whether or not the file was stamped. Left: what a downloaded or reposted copy shows (baked only). Middle: on-site, file stamped (HTML label covers the baked mark). Right: on-site, legacy unstamped file (HTML label supplies the visible label by itself).

2. Rules (if image width, then label)

If displayed image width isLabel textMax charsTool name on expand
under 96 pxnone (metadata only)0none
96 to 199 px"AI"2none (aria-label only)
200 to 319 px"AI-generated"12none (aria-label only)
320 px and up"AI-generated"12up to 16 chars, then an ellipsis

Label width never exceeds 70% of the image width (max-width: 70cqw). The stamping script applies the same thresholds to the source file, using the width the image is displayed at most often; it stamps "AI-generated" on any source 200 px or wider.

3. Small-image matrix (mocked, to scale)

Each column is a real pixel width. Row 1: the baked mark alone, proportional (3.2% of width, capped at 14 px, no floor). Row 2: the on-site label, between 9 px and 14 px type. Row 3: expanded with a 16-char tool name where the rules allow. Text is chosen by the rules above.

4. Annotations

ItemSpec
One component.aiLabel in the design system. The stamping script reads the same values (anchor, padding ratio, border, fill) from one shared config, so the two cannot drift.
AnchorLower-left, 3% of image width in from the left and bottom edges. One position for both; there is no lower-right badge any more.
SizeType is 3.2% of image width, held between 9 px and 14 px on-site (amended 2026-10-30: the first draft had no ceiling, which gave about 61 px type on a 1920 px hero). The baked mark has the same 14 px cap and no floor, so the on-site label is never smaller than it and covers it.
FillOne dark pill on every image (midnight token, white text, chip border). No light variant, so both layers always look the same.
RevealHover or keyboard focus expands the tool name. Tap toggles on touch. Esc or blur closes. 200 ms transition, none under reduced motion.
AccessibilityFocusable, role="img", aria-label "AI-generated image" plus the tool name when known. Focus ring uses the accent token. The baked layer is decorative on-site (aria-hidden).
WhereInline images, article, node and case study heroes, card thumbnails. Gallery images are out of scope. On cards the label follows the same width rules; the tool name never expands (the card is a link).
Schema consequenceThe covering rule works whether or not the file is stamped, so SUG-178 needs no "is stamped" field. ST-178 may still add one for the Studio guard.
Not a nav surfaceNo scroll-spy, sticky or hash behaviour. Mobile: same label, tap to expand.
